chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is it permissible to give food as a loan (salam) to a man who has no food and no livestock, except that when the due date arrives, he buys it and fulfills the obligation? He said: 'If he guarantees it to a specified term, there is no harm.'
I said: What do you think if he fulfills part of it and delays part of it? He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.يُسْلِمَ: To give as a salam loan (pre-payment for specific goods)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on giving food as a loan (salam) to someone who does not currently possess it?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the conditions of the *bay' al-salam* (forward sale) contract, specifically addressing the permissibility of pre-paying for goods when the seller currently lacks inventory but guarantees future delivery. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the contract provided the delivery date is specified, and notably permits partial fulfillment with delayed payment for the remainder, reflecting the practical flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in commercial transactions.
